about: ADR-0208: the rows the Definition of Done checks by hand, the code each covers, and each row's latest record. A row's record holds while its paths are unchanged between the commit the record was made at and the commit being signed off; the release workflow checks it (tools/release/ExGrid.Release, ByHand) and refuses a version without a suffix, and a release candidate, when a row's paths changed since its record, when its latest record is not a pass, when it has none, or when the record's commit cannot be fetched through its tag. The rows and paths are the Definition of Done's Step 4 table, 'Rows checked by hand, and the code each covers', word for word: tests/ExGrid.Release.Tests holds the two together. A path is a file, a directory ending in /, or a pattern written :(glob)<pattern>, which git reads as a glob. A record is the file under verification/ that gives the row's verdict; 'commit' is the commit it names as verified, in full; 'tag' is the tag the run put on that commit and pushed, 'verified/' followed by the name of the record's directory under verification/ and nothing else, one tag per record directory, whatever the platform or the run's purpose: verification/2026-10-01-windows-browser-11/keys.md is tagged verified/2026-10-01-windows-browser-11 (2026-10-12, decided with the user); the release workflow refuses a record whose tag is not exactly that, and fetches the commit through it. A run that records a row replaces its record here, in the same commit as the record; 'record' is null for a row never recorded. WR-10's row is the Wrappers' MudBlazor floor run of Step 4, an automated run a person makes once and its record carries forward while its paths are unchanged (ADR-0205's note of 2026-10-12). Its record, and only its, names besides in 'versions' the MudBlazor versions its layer-2 runs covered, as ['9.6.0', '9.7.0'] (2026-10-12, decided with the user: a MudBlazor 9.x published after the floor record and before X asks for the layer-2 runs at that version only, and the floor run holds while its paths are unchanged). The release workflow lists the stable versions nuget.org's flat-container index gives within the range the Wrappers' projects declare on their PackageReference to MudBlazor, and refuses the tag naming each one the record does not name, or as unchecked when the list cannot be read. 'note' is for a reader and is not read by the check.

The Wrappers' MudBlazor floor run of Step 4 and the layer-2 runs across the declared range beside it (ADR-0205's notes of 2026-10-12): automated, made once by a person on a desktop with Chrome and Edge installed, and carried forward by its record while the Wrappers and the demo pages are unchanged; a MudBlazor 9.x published after it asks for the layer-2 runs at that version only, which its record's 'versions' then names (decided with the user, 2026-10-12).
